Welcome to Mulberry Academy Bexhill
Our school is proud to serve a vibrant, dynamic, and diverse community of around 1,500 students.
While we are dedicated to helping every student discover their unique talents and strengths, our mission remains simple: we put learning at the heart of everything we do to create the very best opportunities for each and every student.
To achieve this, we are fortunate to have a caring, talented, and dedicated team of staff who work tirelessly to support, inspire, and educate the young people entrusted to us. We are proud of our strong connections with the wider community, and we are consistently inspired by how our students embrace the rich experiences we strive to provide.
This powerful sense of collective responsibility is the foundation of all that we achieve together, shaping an environment where every student can flourish – academically, personally, and socially.
Dr Craig Neal Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Music & Performing Arts Tuition
A place to be seen, heard, and celebrated.
Our music and performing arts tuition offers students the opportunity to explore instrumental music, singing, and drama and communication in a supportive and inspiring environment.
As an accredited centre for London College of Music examinations, we open doors to recognised qualifications while nurturing creativity, confidence, and a lifelong love of the arts.
Our Instructors
Alex Rumble
Alex, has been playing guitar professionally since 2006. Has toured the UK and Europe multiple times as a session musician for rock and pop artists as well as with his own bands, including performing at some of the world’s biggest festivals.
Alex gained BA Hons degree in Professional musicianship from the Brighton institute of modern music and has been teaching guitar for 8 years. Alex loves to teach students through the music they love.
Joshua Cole
Joshua Cole is a professional guitarist with nearly a decade of performance experience across the country, performing in a variety of ensembles and styles including funk, rock, and fingerstyle guitar.
In addition to performing, he is skilled in composition and music production.
As an educator, Joshua works with students at every stage – from complete beginners to those writing and recording their own original nusic. He emphasizes student-led learning, encouraging students to bring their own musical interests into lessons.
His philosophy is simple: there’s no better way to learn than by playing the music you love.
Jon Ewen
Jon Ewen is an independent drummer and educator with over 40 years of playing experience, including 35 years performing and teaching professionally.
Alongside his independent work, Jon is a member of the 70s hard rock-influenced band Mars Bonfire, who are currently writing their debut album, with live dates expected in late 2025 and early 2026.
He also performs with rock covers band Admiral Finns Reloaded and folk trio Llama Legs, showcasing his versatility across genres.
Keren Moore
Keren trained at the BRIT School of Performing Arts and Technology and is a qualified ISTD Tap Dance Teacher. She also holds a recognised vocal teaching accreditation through the AOTOS Vocal Teacher Development Essentials course and is currently studying for a Level 5 Diploma in Singing Teaching.
She has extensive teaching experience across musical theatre, singing, drama and dance, including tap, ballet, jazz, contemporary and commercial styles. Her students regularly take part in Trinity Musical Theatre and Speech & Drama exams, LAMDA, LCME assessments and local performance festivals. Keren also choreographs, directs and produces for amateur productions.
In 2022, Keren appeared on Britain’s Got Talent with The Frontline Singers, performing at the London Palladium and later in the televised semi-final at the Hammersmith Apollo. She has also performed for the Katie Piper Foundation Christmas Concert, appeared on Crimewatch Live, and recorded at Abbey Road Studios.
Before returning to the performing arts full-time, Keren served as a Police Officer for nearly 15 years before moving into education, including work as a Primary School Teaching Assistant.
Keren now teaches 1-to-1 drama lessons, supports productions at Bexhill Academy, runs her own coaching business, and performs regularly as an events and wedding singer with her bands Keren and the Condiments and Soul Town.
Hana Lewis
Hana Lewis is a professional singer and vocal coach with nearly 20 years of experience in the music industry. She trained at BIMM, achieving a Distinction Vocal Diploma, and completed specialist speech-level singing training with Lloyd Wade.
Alongside her performing career, Hana has over 15 years of teaching experience, working with students aged five to adult. She supports singers of all abilities, focusing on healthy technique, confidence, musicality and performance skills. She has extensive experience preparing students for musical theatre and popular vocal examinations, as well as local competitions.
Hana has worked with major record labels including Universal and has written and recorded original music, including an EP. One of her songs continues to raise funds for Age UK, with all profits donated to the charity.
As a performer she has toured across the UK, Ireland, Scotland, the South of France and the Mediterranean. She has worked on the West End stage at the Lyric Theatre with John Maher and the lead choreographer from Thriller Live, and has performed in both Celine Dion and ABBA tribute productions, including ABBA Inferno. She continues to perform regularly and has headlined the Hastings Music Festival on multiple occasions.
Alongside performing, Hana remains passionate about developing confident, healthy singers and supporting the next generation of performers.

Computer Science
Hands-on coding, cybersecurity, and tech skills, preparing students to create, innovate, and lead in the fast-changing digital world.
In a world driven by technology, Computer Science at Bexhill Academy equips students to be creators, not just consumers. The course covers coding, cybersecurity, data handling, and computational thinking, alongside software development and emerging technologies. Students gain hands-on experience with programming languages, problem-solving challenges, and real-world tech applications, building both logical reasoning and creative solutions. With expert guidance and a focus on innovation, this course prepares students for further study, careers in the fast-moving tech sector, and a future where digital skills are essential.

Why take part in work experience?
Taking part in work experience offers students a really valuable opportunity to experience the world of work, and encouraging young people to step out of their comfort zone is so important. It encourages them to think about what sort of job and work environment might suit them and to then reflect on the skills and experience that are needed for the work place. It is something really positive that students can include in their CV or personal statement, and it gives them something to talk about at interviews. Above all it can really help to develop confidence, a sense of responsibility and independence.

(Gatsby Benchmark 2 – Learning from career and labour market information)
Labour Market Information (or LMI) can be a confusing concept to begin with but in truth, it’s much simpler than you might think.
LMI can help visual what the job market is like in a particular area of the country, or in a particular industry. It can outline how many people in a given area work within a particular industry (such as manufacturing, or health and social care) and which industries are set to grow in the next few years. This can be very useful when looking at changing careers, or planning future career ideas as it helps identify the likelihood of finding local opportunities in the future.
It can also show the average wages for a location or industry and average working hours to help you make well informed future decisions.
The expert advisers at the National Careers Service can help you understand the LMI in your area for free- call anytime between 8am and 10pm everyday on 0800 100 900 for free, impartial advice.

Futuready
Latest research shows that as well as online support, young people want face-to-face advice and guidance from businesses when they are starting to think about their future career. Building on our work to improve our students career aspirations, we are working with local business Hastings Direct, so that our Year 9 and 10 students can experience Futuready, a programme of inspirational events focussing on happiness, confidence, hope, relationships and employability.
A collaboration between Hastings Direct and social enterprise Humanutopia, the Futuready Programme positively impacts and shapes the future workforce at the same time as offering businesses a fantastic opportunity to make a tangible, measurable and life changing difference to local young people. Futuready focusses on qualities and life skills that support qualifications and success. In a mixture of larger group work, smaller breakout groups and 1-2-1 sessions, the young people and business volunteers are able share their views, day-to-day issues and concerns, and aspirations for the future. The students are invited to look at the influences of others, peer pressure and the culture of conformity and will reflect on their attitude, behaviour and impact on themselves and others.
Futuready helps young people to understand what positive changes they need to make in order to realise their aspirations and what qualities are required to be successful in business and the workplace. Business volunteers from Hastings Direct provide support and advice throughout the Futuready journey, acting as positive role models and guides, and helping to inspire the students with their ideas and encouragement.
Bringing the corporate community to students who are preparing for their next career steps, Futuready is designed to support young people on their life journey and open their eyes to the world of work and the possibilities it can bring.

Mulberry Academy Bexhill is governed by the Mulberry Schools Trust. The Local Governing Body (LGB) is responsible for the oversight of the school and for the implementation of the Mulberry School Trust’s policies and strategy. You can read more about the Mulberry Schools Trust, its Board of Trustees, its policies and the shared work between schools by following the links at the end of this page.
Christine Bayliss
Christine Bayliss is a leading Education Consultant supporting schools, academies and Multi-Academy Trusts on project management, governance, school marketing and PR. She set up her consultancy company CBECS in 2015 following 15 years’ service as a Civil Servant in the Department for Education. Her experience in Whitehall included spells at HM Treasury advising Ministers on Children’s services and on secondment to Manchester City Council serving as an Assistant Chief Education Officer developing the City’s education strategy ‘High Standards for All’.
Christine has lived nearly all her adult life in Bexhill and is a local district councillor serving on Rother’s cabinet as lead for Economic Development and Regeneration. She has two grown-up children who both attended Bexhill High School – the predecessor school to Bexhill Academy. Christine is also a Trustee of Aurora Academies Trust which runs Glenleigh Park and King Offa Primary Schools in Bexhill.
Ralph Cohen
Governor + Ralph is a qualified Solicitor. His legal career has spanned 35 years working as a commercial lawyer in two of the City of London’s leading law firms, including postings to Hong Kong and Brussels. He has represented international clients in some of the largest commercial and trade disputes involving the European Commission and domestic competition authorities.
He served as Managing Partner at his last law firm for nine years, gaining considerable management experience. During that time he lead the firm through a period of significant growth and expansion across Europe.
Ralph is also a qualified Mediator in dispute resolution and an accredited Executive Coach.
He is married with three sons.

SEND & Inclusion
At Bexhill Academy, we are proud to be an inclusive school where every student is valued, supported, and encouraged to achieve their full potential. We are committed to providing a high-quality education for all, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Our approach is rooted in our core values: Aspirational, Collective Responsibility, and Firm but Fair.
We believe that every child deserves access to a broad, balanced, and ambitious curriculum, and we work tirelessly to remove barriers to learning so that all students can thrive. Whether through in-class support, targeted interventions, or our specialist autism provision, The LINK, we tailor our support to meet the individual needs of each learner.
Our SEND provision is led by Mr Mike Walton, Assistant Headteacher and SENCO, supported by a highly skilled team including a Deputy SENCO, Assistant SENCO, Intervention Leads, and Teaching Assistants. We also work closely with a range of external professionals to ensure that our students receive the best possible support.
We follow the graduated approach to SEND support-assess, plan, do, review-ensuring that provision is responsive, evidence-based, and centred around the student and their family. We value strong partnerships with parents and carers and believe that collaboration is key to student success.
Our SEND Information Report and SEND Policy provide detailed information about how we identify, support, and monitor students with SEND. You can explore these documents below or contact our SEND team directly if you have any questions or would like to discuss your child’s needs.
We look forward to working with you to ensure that every student at Mulberry Academy Bexhill feels safe, supported, and empowered to succeed.

Amaze SENDIASS is the Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Information, Advice and Support Service for East Sussex and Brighton & Hove. Amaze SENDIASS is funded by East Sussex County Council and Brighton & Hove City Council to offer impartial and confidential information, advice and support on anything to do with SEND including education, health and social care. The service is for children and young people with SEND up to 25 who live or go to school in East Sussex and Brighton & Hove, and their parents and carers.
Amaze SENDIASS provides information, advice and support in the following ways:
The advice line is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Email sendiass@amazesussex.org.uk or leave a voicemail on 01273 772289. Parents can also ask for help by completing a registration form on the website.
Holding Space offers parent peer support to families whose children are struggling with their mental health. They offer a safe, confidential, non-judgemental space for parents to come together where parents can connect, chat and be supported. They run informal coffee mornings and evenings which are facilitated by parents with lived experience. They have information on local and statutory organisations that can offer support and advice and can signpost to these. They run workshops on mental health and well-being so that they can empower parents to manage their own mental health and those around them.

Home/Remote Learning
At Bexhill Academy, we believe that high-quality home learning, completed independently by our students outside the timetabled curriculum, has a strong positive impact on their progress.
It helps our students reach their full potential and develop into flexible, independent learners capable of managing the demands of future working life.
We are so committed to this belief that the tasks we set are designed for our students to learn at home, not just work at home. This distinction is why we use the term Home Learning alongside Homework.
Benefits of Home Learning
Consolidates and extends knowledge covered in lessons.
Prepares our students for new learning activities.
Encourages personal research and curiosity.
Fosters parental support and engagement.
Strengthens home-school communication.
KS3 Homework Guide for Parents
KS4 Homework Guide for Parents
Setting on Edulink
Home Learning will be set in a variety of ways or on a variety of platforms; Google Classroom, paper copies, Seneca, Hegarty Maths etc. depending on what is most suitable.
However, in order for it to be a clear task for students and parents/carers to see, it will always be signposted on EduLink.
Students will be awarded positive and negative points for the submission of their Home Learning. All of these, as well as the tasks set, can be viewed from the EduLink parent app.
Key Stage 3
Students will be provided with Home Learning weekly in the following subjects:
English, Maths, Science, History, Geography, and Languages
Home Learning tasks should last approximately 30 minutes. Any longer activities or tasks will be broken down into smaller accessible chunks to support students.
In all other subjects, students will be provided with home learning twice per term.
Homework Schedule
Key Stage 4
Students will be provided with home learning weekly in all subjects:
English, Maths, Science, and in each of their option subjects
Home Learning tasks should last approximately 30-45 minutes. Any longer activities or tasks will be broken down into smaller accessible chunks to support students.
Homework Club
There are support sessions that run in the library after school each day for all students 3:00pm-4:00pm. This is a great opportunity for your child to get their home learning done with extra support if needed.
Many departments also offer their own subject specific clubs, speak to your child’s subject teacher for more information on these.

Parents
Strong partnerships between school and parents are essential for student success. At Bexhill Academy, we believe that collaboration between parents and teachers plays a crucial role in providing the best possible education. We highly value parental feedback, as it helps us continuously improve and enhance the learning experience for our students.
To maintain open lines of communication, we host termly parent forums where parents can share their thoughts, concerns, and ideas. We also send out regular parent surveys to gather feedback on various aspects of school life.
Accessibility is a priority, and parents are encouraged to reach out to our dedicated Year Teams or the school office at office@bexhillacademy.org if they have any questions or need assistance. By working together, we can create an environment where every student can thrive and reach their full potential.
We also hold high expectations for our pupils, believing that academic and personal success begins with a readiness to learn. This means coming to school with a positive attitude, a willingness to engage, and the confidence to take on new challenges. We encourage students to arrive prepared, both mentally and physically, and to actively participate in classroom activities. By fostering a mindset of readiness, we empower our students to make the most of their education and achieve their goals.

Catering
Please see the following suggestions from our Catering Manager, Sarah.
Harrisons Catering
If you have not had money put on the School Gateway app, you can pay cash into the school canteen before tutor time. We advise this to be done when you first come to school, so you can go straight to the tills at break or lunch as your money will be available.
If you are entitled to FSM this will not show up on the School Gateway, it will only show when you go to the till. It will always take from the FSM account first when you purchase items and the value is £2.80 per day. It is best to save that for lunchtime, as if you spend it before, there will be none left on the account for lunchtime.
We have two kiosks outside, one in each playground; a variety of items, with hot food, cold food and drinks. Ice lollies and cookies are also available.
Every week at lunchtime:
We’re proud to provide a variety of options each day so that every student can find something they enjoy.
The main menu will be up on the counter from breakfast time so that you have a chance to think about what you might like for lunch.
Please do speak to Sarah (She wears a white coat!) or any member of her team – they are always happy to help.
